clue.text: Court request collected works — has to involve President first

indicators.note: first says this assembled part leads, ahead of the works named at the start of the clue
to involve something is to take it in, so one word wraps around another here

parts.note: taken as written, to be split around the next piece
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US President
a corpus is the whole body of a writer's works

explanation.surface: A lawyer files a court request while a President's collected writings sit in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe is the familiar short name of Abraham Lincoln, so 'President' is a common crossword route to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A habeas corpus writ is a legal demand that a detained prisoner be brought before judges.

clue.text: Item that fixes part of cooker having new trouble

parts.note: a hob is the cooking surface on top of a cooker
N is the abbreviation for new
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A repair item for a faulty cooker that has developed fresh trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob is the British word for a stovetop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobnail is a short heavy-headed nail hammered into boot soles, so something used to fasten.

clue.text: Base receiving warning after cream tea curdled — when still edible?

parts.note: the cream is the best of anything

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one word holds another

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation
fore is the golfer's warning shout

indicators.note: curdled milk is spoiled and changed in form, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cream and tea have curdled, raising the question whether they are still safe to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' means the finest of anything, not dairy, and FORE is what golfers shout to warn others of a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The label printed on food packaging shows the deadline before which it remains good to eat.

clue.text: Article from the pen of singular Saint: something deep

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
a book by an author is from their pen
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written by a remarkable saint offers some profound thought.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a bottomless chasm or a very profound pit.

clue.text: Start to climb up to get on piece of furniture

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of climb
taken as written
to board a train is to get on it

explanation.surface: Someone begins to clamber up onto a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a cabinet with shelves and doors for storing things, a common household fixture.

clue.text: Dance very unnecessary in party

indicators.note: what is unnecessary can be dispensed with, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a revel is a lively celebration
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Dancing at a party is declared quite unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance performed in sets.

clue.text: Fail to stress indication of softness in some carpeting?

indicators.note: in places the musical letter inside the flooring word

parts.note: underlay is the padding laid beneath a carpet, an example of carpeting, hence the question mark
p for piano is the musical mark meaning play softly

explanation.surface: Someone fails to emphasise how soft a carpet feels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' joins the piece to the carpeting; in a music score p tells the player to go quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To underplay something is to downplay or understate its importance, giving it little emphasis.

clue.text: Policeman redirected persons to crime

indicators.note: redirected means sent a new way, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An officer steers people towards crime instead of away from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and a long-running British TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is a fictional police detective, so he is one example of an officer of the law.

clue.text: Exploit upset the person writing this procedure

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down entry flips the word bottom to top

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a ploy is a tactic or manoeuvre

explanation.surface: The writer is upset at being exploited by some procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to use it or make use of it for one's own purposes.

clue.text: Dominant kid grabbing Pole repeatedly

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold of, so the child word clutches the pole letters inside it

parts.note: a kid is a young lad
S is the south pole, and repeatedly asks for it twice

explanation.surface: A domineering child snatches something from a Polish classmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bossy is domineering, always telling others what to do, so dominant in manner.

clue.text: £25, including fees returned by Mike Carroll?

indicators.note: by means next to here, so the final letter is placed alongside the rest
including means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: dues are fees paid, for example for membership
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike Carroll pays twenty-five pounds, fees included, back to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Dodgson, hence the question mark: Carroll is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll is the assumed literary name used by Charles Dodgson, a classic writer's alias.

clue.text: A cry for help about worst poisonous substance

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the distress call wraps the verb

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
to worst someone is to defeat them, as is to best them

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for help as a toxic material threatens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was used in building insulation until its dust was found to cause lung disease.

clue.text: Move poet to pen right line

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as an animal in a pen, so one letter is held inside

parts.note: Alexander Pope, the eighteenth-century poet
R is the abbreviation for right
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A poet is urged to write the correct line with his pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing instrument for the poet, but it means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel something is to drive or push it forward, causing it to travel.

clue.text: Person possibly given documentation after prison sentence

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another, setting the order of the two parts

parts.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term
a form is an official document to fill in

explanation.surface: A prisoner given a life term is handed paperwork to sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is one example of a living organism, and 'possibly' signals the example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Dodgy story supported by account provided by one mathematician

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
on means resting upon, so supported by; in a down clue it sits below
ACC is the abbreviation for account
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A mathematician's account of events turns out to be a dodgy story.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibonacci was a medieval Italian scholar of numbers, famous for his sequence.

clue.text: Courageous and fortunate in pursuit of power

indicators.note: something in pursuit of another follows behind it, so it comes second

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
fortunate means having good luck

explanation.surface: A brave, lucky person chases after power.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means showing pluck, that is spirited bravery in the face of difficulty.

clue.text: Alfred picked up expression of sadness about King in sudden gathering

indicators.note: picked up means lifted, which in a down entry turns the word upward

parts.note: Alf is short for Alfred

indicators.note: about means around, so the sad word goes around the royal letters

parts.note: a sob expresses grief
HM stands for His Majesty

explanation.surface: Alfred heard someone sigh about the King amid an unexpected crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a sound cue, but in a down clue it means turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash mob is a crowd that assembles abruptly in public, performs, then disperses.

clue.text: Writer's one book covered in a lot of rubble

indicators.note: something covered in another is buried inside it, so it sits within
a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a slope
B is the abbreviation for book
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A writer's only book lies buried under a heap of rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, historically a copyist of manuscripts before printing.

clue.text: Scrutinise attention in school

indicators.note: in places one word inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A teacher demands close attention and examination in class.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to examine carefully and thoroughly, looking for something.

clue.text: Bet success will be welcomed by a theatre fan

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken in, so the earlier pieces sit inside

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
to lay a bet is to wager
to make a go of something is to succeed at it

explanation.surface: A gambler's winning bet is greeted by an enthusiastic theatre audience member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like the article but stands for PER, as in prices quoted 'a' or 'per' item.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgoer regularly attends dramatic performances, so is a devotee of the stage.

clue.text: Catwalk is home to a fugitive

indicators.note: a home holds its occupant, so the second word lives inside the first

parts.note: a runway is the raised walkway in a fashion show
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fugitive hides out on a fashion show catwalk.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway is someone who has fled or escaped, so one who is on the run.

clue.text: Intense skill, circling where animal hides

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: An intense hunter circles the lair where a creature is hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent describes passionate, fervent feeling, which is strong or intense emotion.

clue.text: A youngster rejected fame without disagreement

parts.note: taken as written
a son is a young male child

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to have a name is to be famous

explanation.surface: A young person turns down fame without any argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a group acting in complete unity, every member agreeing simultaneously.

clue.text: Egg on something explosive

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
re means on, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: Someone urges on an act that turns out to be explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' looks like the phrase meaning urge, but the two words are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, the main ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Worker in cloth often runs from laundromat machine

indicators.note: from means taken away from, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a tumble dryer is found in a laundromat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cloth worker often runs out of the launderette with the machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of DRYER; 'often' is part of the definition, since textiles are a frequent but not sole material.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer colours fabric and yarn by soaking it, so commonly works with textiles.

clue.text: Unduly sentimental, though not about son being involved in river disaster

indicators.note: in places everything gathered so far inside the next word

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: being involved means joining in, so the next letter is added to the trimmed word
though not says the word that follows is to be left out

parts.note: treacly means cloyingly sweet, figuratively over-sentimental
re means about, concerning
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.walkthrough: Treacle is the British name for golden syrup or molasses, so treacly means sickly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a sudden violent upheaval, a calamity on a huge scale.

clue.text: Shy, cut short the argument

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
a row is a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid, but it is the verb, as in a coconut shy.

clue.text: "Fancy beer," I crow, "runs in my place for making it"

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the final word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A brewer boasts that his fancy beer flows freely at his own place where it is made.
